summary: Nora now says she cannot listen to a voice note, instead of saying it isn't a picture.
detail: Tag her on a voice note or a video and she used to answer that it wasn't a photo — true, but the wrong thing to say, because it made a gap in her wiring sound like a fact about your message. She now tells you plainly that she can't take that in, and keeps 'that's a file I can't open' for things nothing could ever read. Underneath, the machinery that describes a picture has been split so audio and video can each have their own model. Both are switched off in this release and nothing about her behaviour with pictures changes; when a model that can hear or watch is available, turning it on is a setting, not new code.
limitations: She still cannot actually hear a voice note or watch a video. This release only builds the path and the honest answer for not having one.
Speech-to-text is deliberately not part of this — transcribing what somebody said is a different kind of service, and a full transcript needs its own thought about what it might repeat out loud.
